title: Risotto al Pomodoro
subtitle: A slow-stirred tomato risotto with parmesan
excerpt: Ripe tinned tomatoes cooked into a soft, creamy risotto. Each ladleful of stock is stirred in slowly so the rice releases its starch and the sauce becomes thick and glossy. A simple supper that rewards patience.
sourceNotes: Classic northern Italian tomato risotto, synthesised from traditional Lombardy and Piedmont methods.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The base soffritto can be made a day ahead. Cook the risotto fresh to serve.

content.text: This is a quiet tomato risotto that needs stirring and time. Add the stock one ladleful at a time and do not rush. The starch from the rice builds the sauce as you go.
Keep the stock hot in a medium saucepan over a low heat. You need it simmering throughout.
Warm the olive oil in the large saucepan over a medium-low heat. Add the onion and a pinch of salt. Cook gently for 8 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes until the grains look slightly glassy at the edges.
Pour in the wine and stir until absorbed. Add the tinned tomatoes and stir well. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the hot stock one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly and wait until each ladle is absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18 to 20 minutes in total.
When the rice is tender but still has a little bite, remove the pan from the heat. The mixture should flow slowly when you tilt the pan.
Stir in the cold butter and parmesan quickly. Cover and rest for 2 minutes. Taste for salt, add black pepper, and serve with basil leaves on top.

items.symptom: The rice is stodgy and gluey.
items.cause: Too much stirring with high heat or the stock was added too fast.
items.fix: Add a splash more hot stock and stir gently to loosen before serving.

items.symptom: The rice is still chalky after 20 minutes.
items.cause: The stock was not hot enough, slowing absorption.
items.fix: Keep adding hot stock a little at a time and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more.

items.symptom: The risotto is too thick before the rice is done.
items.cause: Too little stock was prepared or it was added too slowly.
items.fix: Add hot water in small amounts, stirring between each addition.
